newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria to step up security to guard elections.
newsitem.headline: Algeria to step up security to guard elections.

text.p: Algeria, after four days of bloodshed in which about 160 people died, will tighten security to thwart any Moslem rebel attacks against voters in the June 5 parliamentary election, Algerian prime minister said on Monday.

"The authorities will step up security measures to ensure the forthcoming ballot is held in a peaceful atmosphere," Ahmed Ouyahia was quoted by the official media as telling a news conference in Algiers.
Ouyahia hailed the solidarity shown by foreign countries, including the United States, for Algeria's fight against "barbaric and savage terrorism".
"The latest massacres perpetrated by terrorists have no precedents through the centuries and across the continents," said Ouyahia.

Moslem rebels hacked to death at least 135 villagers in two hamlets within 24 hours last week, the worst killings in the country's five years of violence. Shortly afterwards a bomb on a railway line killed at least 21 people.
At least 200 foreign observers from the United Nations, the Organisation for African Unity and the Arab League will monitor the poll, said Ouyahia.
The government has allowed foreign observers as well as thousands of local party activists to watch the poll process in order to allay opposition fears that the authorities could rig the elections.

President Liamine Zeroual sees the parliamentary election as a way out of the crisis which erupted after the authorities in January 1992 cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead.
Since then about 60,000 people have been killed.

Ouyahia, who is standing for the 380-seat National Assembly alongside about 8,000 other candidates from more than 40 political parties, vowed to continue fighting the guerrilla movement until all rebels were wiped out.
And in an apparent reference to the recent massacres, he added: "The blows dealt to terrorism are squeezing the terrorists to increase their barbaric and vile acts."
